A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iJKOnet work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic potential and interaction recovery experiments and single-cell prediction results, including Table 1 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v2 reports original iJKOnet results on synthetic energy recovery and EB/Multiome single-cell data in Section 5 and Appendix B. Some comparator scores are explicitly attributed to other papers.

M1.justification: The main objectives and energy parameterization are retained. However, v2 Appendix C.2 reports separate transport networks per timestep for large tasks, whereas v1 used one shared time-conditioned network. Algorithm 1 also corrects the energy-update reference from the current snapshot to the next snapshot, consistent with the already stated objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds the Multiome dataset alongside EB and introduces diffusion-coefficient recovery under the full energy parameterization. Its unpaired potential evaluation expands from six challenging potentials to the fifteen already represented in v1's paired evaluation. These substantially broaden the evaluated data and recovery tasks.

E2.justification: v1's EB comparison contains only JKO-based comparators. v2 Table 5 retains these and adds Neural SDE, TrajectoryNet, SB-FBSDE, NLSB, OT-CFM, WLF-OT and WLF-SB. Tables 1–2 additionally compare against Vanilla-SB, DMSB, MMSB and MIOFLOW. v2 explicitly attributes the non-JKO scores to prior publications.

E3.justification: v2 introduces EB leave-two-out evaluation in 5D with Wasserstein-2 distance, leave-one-out/all-time evaluation in 100D with MMD, and Multiome leave-one-out evaluation in 50D/100D. The reported large-sample unpaired setting changes from 20K to 10K, and interaction ground truths are explicitly symmetrized. The new internal-energy experiment tests diffusion levels 0, 0.1 and 0.2 in 2D/20D.

E4.justification: v2 adds diffusion-recovery analysis across dimensions and diffusion levels, and revises interaction recovery with symmetric kernels and quantitative sample-size comparisons. It removes v1 Figure 2(d)'s convergence/variability analysis and Appendix B.2 Setup II/Figure 4, which tested whether adding an interaction component harms recovery of purely potential dynamics.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports uncertainty values and statistics from five runs; the corresponding v2 Table 5 gives point estimates without uncertainty or a run count. New v2 Tables 2 and 6 specify three-run averages. This changes reporting, but does not establish that retained experiments were reduced from five runs to three.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results and revises existing ones. For example, the retained EB 5D next-step comparison changes iJKOnet_V's first-transition estimate from 0.87 to 0.92. New Table 2 reports all-time MMD of 0.085 for iJKOnet_V versus 0.032 for DMSB. The diffusion results are newly reported, although their text and Figure 5 disagree on the ranking. The paired-potential plots and paired/unpaired ratio table are retained. Changed experimental conditions elsewhere preclude interpreting revisions as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds convexity of the domain to Theorem 3.1, corrects the internal-energy integrand in Equation (5) from U(x) to U(rho(x)), and states interaction symmetry and boundary/continuity conditions in the background. The recovery bound and Appendix D proof strategy remain substantially the same; the expanded derivation does not constitute a new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal methodological, algorithmic and theoretical contributions are retained. Section 6 adds a claim of comparability with non-JKO methods and strengthens JKO superiority to 'in all comparisons'. This is a limited expansion of the central claims, although Table 2 contains exceptions to the categorical superiority statement.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix A.3 adds an explanation of the paired/unpaired gap through OT sample complexity and estimation variance. Appendix A.2 qualifies the time-varying-potential critique with existing time-dependent JKO theory. Appendix B.2 attributes Multiome failures to long observation intervals, while Section 6 newly identifies time-dependent interaction energies and birth–death dynamics as unsupported. Sample-size benefits are also described less categorically.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents paired synthetic sample/test counts, the EB 60/40 split and 1000-epoch training, and 5000-epoch Multiome training. It expands transport-network and GPU/CPU memory information. These are useful disclosures; the optimizer defaults, basic MLP architecture, entropy estimator and hardware remain largely unchanged, and both versions only promise future code availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning through Appendix A.1's structured discussion of flow/action matching, Schrödinger bridges, unbalanced OT, Riemannian approaches, Wasserstein splines and JKO applications. It also acknowledges concurrent inverse-JKO work by Andrade et al. and distinguishes its unbalanced setting, potential-only scope and sample-complexity focus.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative and appendix organization are extensively revised. Broader related work moves into an expanded discussion appendix, paired synthetic experiments move into Appendix B, and metric definitions move from Appendix A.3 to C.1. v2 adds an appendix contents list and rewrites explanatory passages, alongside author-affiliation and citation-style changes.

P2.justification: v2 adds the introductory schematic and diffusion boxplots, redraws interaction results, and substantially expands and restructures tables. Figure 2 moves into the main text and changes from six to fifteen potential axes, with logarithmic scales for two metrics and removal of the convergence panel. The paired-potential display is retained as Figure 3, while typography, headers and text wrapping also change.

improvement.justification: The broader non-JKO and held-out-time comparisons, corrected interaction-kernel construction, and clearer research positioning make v2's empirical scope more assessable than v1's narrow evaluation. The gain is limited by lost uncertainty in the retained EB table and removal of diagnostic analyses. New reporting inconsistencies also weaken confidence: Figure 5's plotted errors contradict its written ranking, and Section 6's blanket JKO-superiority claim exceeds Table 2's evidence. The stronger comparative context supports a limited overall improvement despite these weaknesses.
